description: A 2018 survey found 24% of doctoral students reported experiencing abuse of power from their supervisors. Another found 21% had experienced bullying, with 48% identifying supervisors as the most frequent perpetrators - and rates of bullying higher in academia than in other workplaces.
energy_note: A quarter of them, and the supervisor is usually who did it.

description: Once a student is far enough in, the supervisor is so entwined with the project as to be indispensable. Leaving means losing funding, lab access, expertise, the reference and the authorship credit needed for a first postdoc.
energy_note: Four years in, and he is load-bearing.

aspect: Universities leave it to the individual
description: Institutions tend to give supervisors freedom to manage the relationship, which provides few barriers against egregious behaviour and no routine observation of it.
energy_note: Nobody else is ever in the room.

aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the meeting that keeps moving
description: Her chapter has been with him eleven weeks. Each fortnight he is about to get to it. In the corridor: 'You're not in a rush, are you? Some people just aren't built for the timeline.' Her funding ends in seven months.
energy_note: Eleven weeks, and the delay is now her temperament.

description: Research found supervisors in insecure positions significantly more likely to engage in bullying, with productivity demands placing pre-full-professor staff at higher risk - so the pressure on him transfers to her.
